items.p: Our new opening hours start on 1 March. From Monday to Friday the café will open an hour earlier, at 7 am, but it will close at 5 pm instead of 6 pm. Weekend hours do not change.
items.q: What is changing on weekdays?
o: The café opens and closes an hour earlier.
The café is closed at weekends.

items.p: Please note: the 8:15 train to Leeds will leave from platform 4 today, not platform 2. Passengers for York should change at Leeds.
items.q: What should passengers going to York do?
o: Take the Leeds train and change there.

items.p: Remote work was once seen as a perk for a lucky few. Today many companies treat it as standard, arguing that it widens the pool of candidates. Critics, however, warn that junior staff may miss out on the informal learning that happens in an office.
items.q: What concern do critics raise?
o: Junior employees may learn less informally.

items.p: The trial was meant to last six months, but the results were so encouraging that the council decided to make the cycle lanes permanent after just three.
items.q: What happened to the cycle lanes?
o: They became permanent earlier than planned.
They were removed after six months.

items.p: Proponents of the four-day week claim it boosts productivity, yet the evidence is mixed: gains reported in small pilots have not always survived once the novelty wore off and workloads were squeezed into fewer days.

items.p: The author's tone throughout is measured rather than polemical; she concedes the merits of opposing views before methodically dismantling them.
items.q: How does the author argue?

items.p: While the drug performed well in laboratory tests, regulators stopped short of approving it, citing the small size of the clinical trial.
items.q: Why was the drug not approved?

items.p: To call the reforms a success would be to mistake the absence of protest for the presence of support.
items.q: What is the writer's point?
o: A lack of opposition does not prove that people approve.

items.p: The memoir is at its best when the author resists the temptation to tie every episode up neatly; the loose ends, paradoxically, are what make it feel true.
items.q: What does the reviewer praise?
o: The author leaves some things unresolved.
Every story has a clear ending.
The book is short and tidy.

items.p: Far from settling the debate, the new data have merely shifted its terms: the question is no longer whether the effect exists, but how large it is.
items.q: According to the text, the new data…
o: changed what is being argued about.
proved that the effect does not exist.
